summary: The retraction decision itself is substantively correct: the user’s Log 07 audit, RETRACTION precedent, Claude audit, and Codex audit all independently support UNSOUND, the current `docs/proofs/umr_data_processing_gamma.md` preserves v0.2 as an explicitly labeled cautionary record, `gap_shape_g4_1.md`’s corrected 10 dB A/B row matches `docs/research/data/gap_shape.csv`, and the WTB PDF in-repo confirms Theorem 12 and Theorem 19 (with no hits for Theorem 26 or 47). However, the branch is not review-clean: a live conclusions document still presents the retracted v0.2 claim as `[COROLLARY pending]`, the WTB renumbering was not completed globally across `docs/`, `pareto_tf_family.md` still contains PM-QKD values that disagree with the backing CSV, and some evidence links/source attributions are not reproducible from the cited paths.

issues.description: This live conclusions document does not perform a clean retraction. After announcing `path γ v0.2 → v0.3 RETRACTED`, it still states the claim’s current rigor as `[COROLLARY pending user sign-off]`, lists upgrade consequences, keeps `若 path γ v0.2 通过 → [COROLLARY]` as an active branch, and records `adversarial containment` as a technical finding. That leaves the retracted v0.2 argument treated as current in the same file, which is exactly the kind of CONJ→COROLLARY overclaim the retraction was meant to prevent.
issues.suggestion: Rewrite this file so every current-state statement reflects v0.3 `[CONJ]` only. If you want to preserve the v0.2 text, move it under an explicitly marked archived/cautionary section (or strike it through) and remove forward-looking upgrade language from the live summary.

issues.description: The WTB theorem-number correction is not globally applied in `docs/`. The in-repo PDF text shows `Theorem 12` for the teleportation-simulable strong converse and `Theorem 19` for the second-order bound, with no `Theorem 26`/`Theorem 47` hits. But `docs/PHASE1_LOG.md` still says `Thm 26`, and `docs/AUTONOMOUS_SESSION_2026-04-21_CONCLUSIONS.md` still says `WTB Thm 47`.
issues.suggestion: Complete the renumbering sweep across live `docs/` files. Historical audit artifacts can keep the old numbers only if they are explicitly framed as discussing prior mis-citations; active logs and conclusion docs should use Thm 12 / Thm 19 or clearly annotate any historical mention.

issues.description: The family-comparison table is numerically inconsistent with its cited backing CSV. At 10 dB it reports PM-QKD `3.80e-4`, but `docs/research/data/tf_family_loss1d.csv:12` gives `2.497405e-04`. The same table also disagrees at 20 dB (`1.45e-4` vs `7.782689e-05` at line 22), 40 dB (`1.63e-5` vs `7.665311e-06` at line 42), and 60 dB (`1.59e-6` vs `6.955986e-07` at line 62).
issues.suggestion: Regenerate this comparison table from the actual source CSV, or cite the correct alternative dataset if this table intentionally uses a different source. Until then, the stated cross-family quantitative comparisons are not auditably reproducible.

issues.description: The reproducibility trail is partially broken. These docs link to `data/...` and `figures/...` paths under `docs/findings`, but the actual CSVs/figures live under `docs/research/data` and `docs/research/figures`. Also, `gap_shape_g4_1.md` says the table values come from `gap_shape.csv`, but that CSV only contains the TF/A/B/PLOB columns, not the candidate-C column shown in the table.
issues.suggestion: Point every evidence link at the real artifact location and cite the exact backing source for each displayed column. For `gap_shape_g4_1.md`, either add candidate-C data to a tracked CSV or state where that column is sourced from.

round_recommendation: First make the retraction globally consistent by fixing `docs/AUTONOMOUS_SESSION_2026-04-21_CONCLUSIONS.md` to current `[CONJ]` state only, then finish the WTB 12/19 renumbering across live `docs/`, and finally resync `docs/findings/pareto_tf_family.md` from its backing CSV and repair the evidence links.
